chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Hawkins and Ray Nance as physical exceptions
summary: Collins thinks some are chemically stronger, citing Hawkins drinking and snorting yet driving to Atlantic City, and saddened by Ray Nance not knowing him.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You were saying that you think some people are physically better able to handle --

Narcotics, yeah. And I always thought that Coleman Hawkins was very strong, because I used to see him snort heroin, drink, all at the same time, and then get in his car and drive to Atlantic City from New York, when we finished. And that was 4:00 o'clock in the morning. You know.
Ray Nance is another person who never seemed to be affected. He got sick when he quit using heroin, because he was doing other things to in a way compensate.
But for many, many years he could take it or leave it.
Use it steadily or you go without it.
He suffered no other -- he was an athlete, he was in top physical condition.
Yeah, but by the same token, Ray and I came up together, and the last time I saw him he didn't know who I was.
Ray's in very bad shape now, (inaudible)

Yeah, I saw him last Christmas, I was in New York, I went to hear a Thad Jones band, and Ray stood right beside me and he gave me that smile. You know, that vacant smile, you know where I know you from someplace. This. So finally -- I wouldn't tell him for a while, and finally I told him who I was and bought him a drink, you know, okay. But now --
But liquor did that to Ray, and (inaudible) the pills and all the substitute things --
Yeah, everything. Ray used heroin, you know, I mean so --
He was on heroin but he was in fine shape.
Well, no, I wouldn't say he was in fine shape, but --
Except for the use of it --
